attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The actual endpoint incidence table G_{ij,v} and the same-theory tail interval tau_nu have not yet been computed for the full regulated hairpin geometry.
steps: Definition/assumption context: this derivation is interpreted inside Reflection-Positivity Closed-Cone Topology; source object: heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulated SU(N) Wilson collar observables W_i(a,delta) for the already-fixed three-hairpin block, with endpoint boxes B_v(r) around hairpin corners.; target object: the corrected Schur-Feshbach null-channel scalar M_nu=M_G+R_nu^{end}+R_nu^{tail} whose positivity promotes the post-H,K OS bridge for this finite block.; Model: four-dimensional Euclidean SU(N) Yang-Mills is regulated by lattice heat-kernel plaquette sheets with gauge-invariant Wilson observables only..
Start with the already-proved finite Schur-Feshbach reduction for the three-hairpin block and keep only the post-H,K connected polarization scalar in the null direction.

Represent each R_{ij} by heat-kernel plaquette-sheet source derivatives of log Z for the reflected Wilson product; the connected logarithm removes Wick-square disconnected contractions from the dangerous term.
Use the previously established null incidence identity to cancel straight-segment nonabelian C_A f f contacts; only endpoint and corner boxes remain.
Project each endpoint four-flux source to the singlet channel. This gives the color factor c_N=(g_a^4/4)(T_F/N)^2 and endpoint cumulants kappa_v contracted with incidences G_{ij,v}.
Contract with the Feshbach null pair weights 2,-4,-4. The endpoint imbalance is D_v=2G_{12,v}-4G_{13,v}-4G_{23,v}.
Since the compact-group small-time kappa_4 is negative, only D_v>0 can make the endpoint contribution negative. Thus 12-dominance, not generic endpoint negativity, is the actual falsifier mechanism.
Split D_v into positive and negative parts and combine the negative part with the positive Gaussian margin M_G to obtain a certified interval gate for M_nu.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a regulator-level reduction and sign gate. It is not a continuum Yang-Mills proof until the endpoint source derivatives, uniform OPE remainders, and cutoff-removal compatibility are certified.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Post-H,K endpoint-box incidence bound for connected Wilson R

assumptions: Model: four-dimensional Euclidean SU(N) Yang-Mills is regulated by lattice heat-kernel plaquette sheets with gauge-invariant Wilson observables only.
Regime: endpoint boxes are disjoint, smaller than the collar scale, and large enough to contain the local hairpin endpoint OPE support.
Uniformity: the fourth-cumulant OPE and the endpoint-tail estimate are uniform in a, delta, and box radius along the chosen continuum passage.
Cancellation input: connected logarithms remove Wick-square Gram terms from the dangerous scalar, and the straight C_A f f contact cancels by the null incidence identity of the three-hairpin block.
Sign input: the compact-group small-time endpoint cumulant has certified interval kappa_v<=0, or else the bound is interpreted with the full interval for kappa_v.
Non-claim boundary: this lemma only handles the endpoint-local R contribution after H,K are known; it does not prove the full Clay mass gap or continuum existence.
definitions: source object: heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulated SU(N) Wilson collar observables W_i(a,delta) for the already-fixed three-hairpin block, with endpoint boxes B_v(r) around hairpin corners.
target object: the corrected Schur-Feshbach null-channel scalar M_nu=M_G+R_nu^{end}+R_nu^{tail} whose positivity promotes the post-H,K OS bridge for this finite block.

controlled interface: the boundary OPE map sending reflected Wilson products to singlet connected four-flux endpoint cumulants kappa_v, with color factor c_N=(g_a^4/4)(T_F/N)^2 and uniform endpoint-tail remainder.

same-theory condition: the heat-kernel regulator, Wilson normalization, collar embeddings, endpoint sources, and cutoff-removal topology are the locked Yang-Mills ones, with no added boundary counterterm or algebra enlargement.
G_{ij,v} is the squared geometric/color incidence of the endpoint source in box B_v for the reflected pair (i,j), after singlet projection.
D_v:=2G_{12,v}-4G_{13,v}-4G_{23,v} is the Feshbach-null endpoint imbalance; D_v^+=max(D_v,0).
kappa_v is the fourth derivative at zero of log Z_v(su_v), hence the connected fourth cumulant of the endpoint Wilson flux source.

equations.label: null_endpoint_contraction
equations.valid_when: Applies after the finite Schur-Feshbach null vector is fixed and one-body, length-linear, Wick-square, and straight f f contributions have been cancelled.

equations.label: safe_interval_gate
equations.valid_when: Valid when each endpoint cumulant interval satisfies kappa_v in [-kappa_v^-,0] and the tail bound controls every omitted corner and off-box contribution.

equations.label: endpoint_falsifier_gate
equations.valid_when: Requires certified interval arithmetic for the same regulated endpoint cumulants and no change of Wilson normalization between collar and target observables.

equations.valid_when: Valid when log Z_v is analytic for |s|<=3h and the eighth source derivative is bounded on that same endpoint box interval.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If endpoint boxes overlap so that kappa_v is not local, if straight f f contact leaves a nonzero null contribution, or if the source-derivative interval makes overline M_nu<0, the lemma demotes the branch.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This attacks the conceptual pressure of turning the connected boundary-OPE polarization R from a symbolic threat into a regulator-level incidence inequality. The hard gate is the certified sign of M_nu; success promotes the finite block, while failure gives a genuine same-theory OS falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For the locked three-hairpin Wilson collar block, the post-H,K connected endpoint polarization is controlled by a signed endpoint incidence imbalance. After Wick-square removal and straight f f cancellation, a negative compact-group kappa_4 is dangerous only on endpoint boxes where the 12 incidence dominates the 13 and 23 incidences by the Feshbach null weights.

assumptions: Regime: every endpoint box contributes to at most one pair type and all active boxes have the same normalized source strength G.
Uniformity: all endpoint cumulants share a certified interval [-kappa_*,0] and all tails are bounded by T_end.
Geometry: orientations are already absorbed into the pair labels, so the Feshbach weights are exactly 2,-4,-4.
Non-claim boundary: this is a stress-test corollary, not the full incidence table for the actual continuum hairpin geometry.
definitions: source object: the same heat-kernel three-hairpin endpoint box family, restricted to univalent disjoint endpoint incidences.
target object: the sign of the scalar post-H,K endpoint contribution in the Feshbach null direction.
controlled interface: integer endpoint counts n_{12}, n_{13}, n_{23} replacing the geometric incidences G_{ij,v} after equal box normalization.
same-theory condition: the endpoint count model is only a compression of the same regulated Wilson source derivatives, not a replacement theory.

equations.label: univalent_imbalance
equations.valid_when: Valid when endpoint boxes are disjoint, univalent, equally normalized, and the Feshbach null weights are the locked three-hairpin weights.

equations.label: equal_box_safety
equations.valid_when: Applies when the compact-group fourth cumulant is nonpositive and equal endpoint counts represent the actual regulated source incidences.

equations.label: twelve_dominance_threshold
equations.valid_when: Requires M_G>T_end, negative endpoint cumulant sign, and no additional positive cumulant or tail term hidden outside the endpoint boxes.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If actual endpoint incidence is not univalent or equal-strength, this corollary is quarantined and the full G_{ij,v} formula must be used.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This gives a falsifier stress case: equal endpoint populations are safe, so any demotion must be driven by certified 12-dominance or a genuinely negative tail.
candidate_lemmas.statement: In the univalent endpoint model where each endpoint box belongs to exactly one reflected pair type with equal normalized incidence, the negative compact-group kappa_4 cannot demote the block unless the 12 endpoint count exceeds twice the combined 13 and 23 counts, up to the positive margin and tail.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot or quarantine if the real endpoint geometry destroys the straight f f cancellation or if endpoint-tail bounds are not uniform in the cutoff.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if the certified lower interval underline M_nu is positive for the actual G_{ij,v}, kappa_v, and tau_nu; demote with a falsifier if the certified upper interval is negative.
control_decision.reason: This branch is not looping: it is now computing the actual post-H,K R/kappa_4 endpoint-box term required by the paper handoff. The hard gate is the sign of M_nu after interval arithmetic.

dependency_updates.description: Replaces symbolic R entries by the same-theory heat-kernel endpoint source derivative kappa_v and incidence imbalance D_v. Prior-art delta: standard OS reflection-positivity and Wilson-loop constructive arguments do not isolate this finite Schur-Feshbach endpoint cumulant gate.
The endpoint reducer depends on the already identified cancellation of straight nonabelian f f contacts in the null incidence channel; the next validation must insert the real endpoint orientations.
Surface definitions of source object, target object, controlled interface, same-theory condition, endpoint incidences, cumulant intervals, and non-claim boundaries for timeline validation.
Uniform tau_nu bounds decide whether the regulator-level endpoint interval is a valid continuum bridge or only a finite cutoff diagnostic.

falsifiers: A certified interval overline M_nu<0 from the same heat-kernel endpoint sources is a direct same-theory falsifier of the finite block.
The straight C_A f f contact could fail to cancel after the real endpoint orientations are inserted, invalidating the incidence-only reducer.
Endpoint-box overlap could create a nonlocal connected cumulant not bounded by tau_nu, defeating the local OPE interface.
The compact-group kappa_4 interval could include a positive component large enough to nullify the 12-dominance interpretation.
A boundary counterterm or Wilson renormalization change needed to define Z_v would violate the same-theory condition.

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: For d near 1 the negative compact-group kappa_4 raises or preserves M_nu; demotion begins only past a 12-dominance threshold determined by M_G, c_N, |kappa|, and the tail interval.
held_fixed_controls: Same regulated Yang-Mills heat-kernel action and gauge-invariant Wilson algebra.
Already computed H,K block and corrected Schur-Feshbach margin M_G.
Null pair weights 2,-4,-4 and the straight f f cancellation identity.
Uniform endpoint-box radius, singlet projection, and finite-difference error bound.
gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The branch has passed H,K and reduced the remaining obstruction to endpoint kappa_4; another abstract OS restatement would loop, while varying endpoint incidence directly tests the promotion/falsifier gate.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: A heat-kernel SU(N) plaquette-sheet three-hairpin Wilson block with disjoint endpoint boxes, fixed Feshbach null vector, and source derivatives f_v(s)=log Z_v(su_v) evaluated by the seven-point fourth-derivative stencil.
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: A uniform endpoint OPE remainder plus same-theory cutoff-removal certificate showing that the finite source derivative intervals converge to the Wilson collar R_nu without boundary counterterms.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: Endpoint dominance ratio d=\sum_v G_{12,v}/(\sum_vG_{13,v}+\sum_vG_{23,v}) while keeping the total endpoint box scale and source norm fixed.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 258 computes the sign mechanism of the remaining post-H,K R term. The negative compact-group endpoint kappa_4 is not by itself a danger; after the valid cancellations, it is multiplied by D_v=2G12-4G13-4G23. Equal endpoint boxes are safe. The conceptual value signal is sharpness: the branch has localized the only remaining demotion mechanism to certified 12-endpoint dominance or a negative tail, a route-changing reduction from abstract OS positivity to finite endpoint source intervals.

escape_conditions: Endpoint incidence has D_v<=0 except for negligible boxes.
Tail interval is smaller than the positive Gaussian margin.
Positive or mixed endpoint cumulants offset the negative compact-group term.
The alleged negative interval uses a boundary counterterm or changed Wilson normalization and is not same-theory.
negative_tactic_decision.exact_negation_or_method_class: Negate endpoint safety by proving overline M_nu<0 from same-theory heat-kernel source derivatives and incidence data.
negative_tactic_decision.next_validation_handoff: Give the validator the G_{ij,v} table, seven-point stencil values for kappa_v, and tau_nu interval so it can test underline M_nu>0 or overline M_nu<0.
negative_tactic_decision.paper_contribution_potential: A finite, regulator-level endpoint cumulant criterion for the first concrete Wilson hairpin block; this differs from standard constructive-QFT positivity arguments by identifying the exact connected R term that can still falsify the same-theory bridge.
proof_obligations: Compute the actual G_{ij,v} table including orientations and singlet color factors.
Certify kappa_v by source derivative stencil or analytic small-time expansion with eighth-derivative error.
Bound tau_nu uniformly in cutoff, collar, and endpoint-box radius.
Verify that the endpoint OPE limit commutes with the regulated OS collar limit.
negative_tactic_decision.reason_for_tactic: The positive margin is already known; the only useful negative tactic is to try to overwhelm it with certified 12-endpoint dominance or a negative tail.
